Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model. With probability \(\pi_i\) an observation is a structural zero; otherwise it comes from an NB2 distribution with mean \(\mu_i\) and dispersion \(\theta\). The count model is \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and the zero model is \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\). The observed-data log-likelihood is maximized by an EM algorithm: the E-step computes the posterior probability \(\tau_i\) that each zero is structural, and the M-steps are a logistic IRLS fit for \(\gamma\) (fractional response \(\tau_i\)) and a weighted NB fit for \((\beta, \theta)\) with prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\). No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional offset for the count model (e.g. log exposure). An offset() term in the count part of the formula also works.

control

A list from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components including coefficients (a list with count and zero), theta, loglik, loglik_trace (log-likelihood at every EM iteration), iter, converged, fitted.values (\((1-\pi_i)\mu_i\)), mu, pi, tau, y, x, z, offset, terms, formula, and call.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
x <- rnorm(n)
structural_zero <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + 0.5 * x))
y <- ifelse(structural_zero == 1, 0,
            rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | x, data = data.frame(y = y, x = x))
fit$coefficients
#> $count
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   1.1014731   0.4487059 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>  -0.8283902   0.5317871 
#> 
fit$theta
#> [1] 2.322346
